chains.title: T (risk) allele increases GATA3 binding at the TOX3 distal enhancer in luminal breast cells
chains.element: EH38E3180851 (dELS, chr16:52565011-52565360; Ensembl regulatory feature ENSR16_9QTBS)
chains.cell_type: Luminal (ER-positive) breast epithelial cells, modelled by MCF7 (ACH-000019)

links.claim: QBiC GATA group G010 passes with all 6 models predicting stronger alt (T) binding (best model GATA2 z 18.65, effect +0.283; GATA3 own model z 10.91; site strength ref 92.3th to alt 98.6th percentile). Within the group GATA3 is chosen because it is by far the most expressed member in MCF7 (346 TPM vs GATA2 12.7 TPM, all others <1 TPM) and because ENCODE GATA3 ChIP-seq in MCF-7 places 5 peaks over this exact position in 3 independent experiments, so GATA3 is the group member demonstrably occupying the site. The allelic direction remains a prediction: no allele-specific ChIP is cited.

The variant is inside an ENCODE distal enhancer-like cCRE (DNase z 4.2, H3K27ac z 6.1; maxima across biosamples, not MCF7-specific) and an Ensembl enhancer feature; GATA3 occupancy in MCF-7 indicates the element is accessible in this cell line.

Open Targets credible sets containing the variant at PIP 1.00 give TOX3 the top L2G score (0.92-0.96), and TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding TSS (17.5 kb). No contact, CRISPR or breast eQTL evidence links the element to TOX3; GTEx finds no significant breast eQTL, so the assignment rests on statistical gene prioritisation and proximity only.
MCF7 expresses GATA3 at 346 TPM and ENCODE GATA3 ChIP peaks at this site come from MCF-7 biosamples, so the predicted occupancy change is realisable in this context.
T is the effect allele for breast cancer at p 2e-240 and for ER-negative and ER-positive subtypes; the chain assumes but does not show that a GATA3-dependent change in TOX3 mediates this association.

chains.title: T allele acts through the FOXA1 pioneer site that overlaps the variant in MCF-7

links.claim: One ENCODE FOXA1 ChIP-seq peak in MCF-7 contains the variant, so FOXA1 occupies this element. FOXA1 has no QBiC-SELEX model among the 997 scored, so no allelic direction can be assigned from binding models; the alt-preferring direction is assumed from the risk-allele framing and is not evidenced.
The variant sits in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE, the chromatin class where pioneer FOXA1 opens chromatin; occupancy in MCF-7 is shown by ChIP.

TOX3 is the top L2G gene (0.92-0.96) for the breast-cancer credible sets containing the variant and the nearest TSS; no looping or perturbation data connect this FOXA1-bound element to TOX3, and no breast eQTL exists.
The only cited FOXA1 occupancy is in MCF-7, a luminal line, so any effect would be restricted to FOXA1-positive luminal cells; no FOXA1 expression value is cited.
T is the breast-cancer risk allele (p 2e-240), with signal in both ER-negative (p 2e-26) and ER-positive (p 1e-13) analyses; the direction of any TOX3 change is not established.

predictions: FOXA1 ChIP in heterozygous cells shows allelic imbalance at chr16:52565276
FOXA1 knockdown, but not GATA3 knockdown, collapses the allelic reporter difference and reduces chromatin accessibility at the element
Accessibility (ATAC) at the element depends on FOXA1
falsified_if: FOXA1 ChIP shows balanced allelic reads
FOXA1 depletion leaves accessibility and TOX3 unchanged while GATA3 depletion does not

chains.title: T allele creates a strong small-MAF (MAFG/MAFK) site that alters output of the TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: The strongest QBiC signal at this site is bZIP group G012: best model is an own model of MAFG (z 71.57, effect +2.788; site strength ref 97.6th to alt 100th percentile) and all 6 passing models agree on alt-gain. I now name MAFG rather than MAFK because MAFG holds the best own model and is expressed in MCF7 (8.48 TPM); MAFK (16.96 TPM) is the more expressed close paralogue and the two are interchangeable at MARE half-sites, so this is a group-level specificity, not a single-TF call.

The site is an active distal enhancer-like cCRE, so a gained MARE-like site could recruit small MAFs; no small-MAF ChIP evidence at this element is cited and the repressive-versus-activating role is unresolved.
TOX3 is the prioritised target by L2G (0.96) and proximity; no data connect a MAF site to TOX3, and no breast eQTL is seen.
MAFK (16.96 TPM), MAFG (8.48 TPM) and MAFB (3.09 TPM) are expressed in MCF7, so the predicted gain of binding is realisable there.
The T allele carries the 16q12 breast-cancer association; a MAF-mediated change in TOX3 is a hypothesis, not shown by any cited data.

predictions: MAFG/MAFK ChIP or EMSA supershift shows T-allele-specific binding absent on C
Small-MAF knockdown changes reporter activity only for the T allele
Reporter direction may be repressive (small-MAF homodimers), opposite to H1/H2
falsified_if: No small-MAF occupancy at the element in MCF7
MAFG/MAFK depletion has no effect on allelic reporter activity or TOX3

chains.title: T allele disrupts an NFAT site, lowering enhancer activity at TOX3

links.claim: QBiC Rel group G026 predicts loss of binding on the alt allele (best model NFATC4 own model z -23.46, effect -1.044; ref 98.0th to alt 70.9th percentile). NFATC3 is named because it is the most expressed member in MCF7 (9.54 TPM vs NFATC4 0.86 TPM), but its own passing z is only -4.28, the weakest in the group, so the TF assignment within the group is poorly supported.
The variant is in an active distal enhancer; loss of an NFAT site could lower or raise activity, since NFAT family members both activate and repress.
TOX3 is the prioritised gene by L2G and proximity; no evidence ties an NFAT site to TOX3 regulation.
NFATC3 is expressed in MCF7 (9.54 TPM); no NFAT occupancy at this element is shown, and GATA3 and FOXA1 are the only TFs with cited ChIP peaks here.
T is the risk allele; no cited evidence sets the sign of the TOX3 change required by this chain, so the direction is an untested assumption.

predictions: Allele-specific binding favours C; the T-allele reporter shows reduced activity relative to C

falsified_if: T-allele reporter activity is equal to or higher than C
No NFAT occupancy at the enhancer in breast cells

grades_v0.reason: The GATA group passes with the alt allele binding more (E17), but this is a QBiC prediction only. GATA3 has no best-model status; its z is 10.91 against GATA2's 18.65. Choosing GATA3 for its 346 TPM expression is a stated reason. Even so, no ChIP or allelic assay is cited.
E03 and E01 show the variant lies in a dELS cCRE with high H3K27ac and DNase z-scores. These are maxima over biosamples, not MCF7-specific, which limits how strongly they support the claim.

Open Targets L2G gives TOX3 0.92-0.96 with PIP 1.00, and TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene (E05, E02). The literature quote E06a is a review annotation. No perturbation or enhancer-promoter link is shown, and the cited review is not strong evidence, so the gene link rests on genetics.
E17 gives GATA3 expression in MCF7 (346 TPM). Nothing cited shows this enhancer is active in MCF7 or that TOX3 is expressed there. The claim that MCF7 is luminal ER+ comes from outside knowledge.

The GWAS p of 2e-240 with T as the effect allele (E04) and the meta-analysis (E06b) support the association. They do not show the mechanism or the direction of the TOX3 effect. Over-claims causality ('driving risk'), but the association link is genetic and strong.

FOXA1 is not in QBiC coverage and no cited evidence mentions FOXA1 binding at this site. E06a only annotates the enhancer variant for TOX3. The claim that FOXA1 is 'repeatedly implicated' is not in the evidence.
The active dELS (E03) is supported, but nothing links it to FOXA1 occupancy. Only chromatin class is offered as the reason.
L2G for TOX3 is supported by E05 and E02. The claim that the enhancer loops to TOX3 is unsupported, since no contact data is cited.
E05 shows brain-restricted weak molecular QTLs, which do not imply luminal specificity. No FOXA1 expression or MCF7 data is cited, and the argument is a non sequitur.

Association with the T allele is supported (E04). The direction 'increased TOX3 raises risk' is not shown, and the claim of a stronger signal in ER-related subtypes is not borne out: ER-negative p 2e-26 against ER-positive p 1e-13.

The strongest QBiC group (E08) has consistent alt-gain across 6 models, but it is a binding prediction only. MAFK was chosen as the most expressed member, which is a stated reason. MAFG holds the best own model, and MAFK is the choice by expression rather than by model.
E03 supports an active enhancer. The prediction of MARE creation, with repressive or NFE2L2-partner roles, is speculative and unsupported by cited data.
TOX3 L2G and proximity are shown (E05, E02), but nothing connects the MAF site to TOX3 regulation.
E08 lists MAFK at 16.96 TPM and MAFG at 8.48 TPM in MCF7, so expression is established. That is expression only, and no occupancy is shown.
The GWAS association is supported (E04). A MAF-mediated TOX3 change underlying it is not shown. The cited E06a does not mention MAF.

G026 predicts alt-loss (E11), but NFATC3 z -4.28 is barely passing and is the weakest of the three. NFATC4 is the best model and the NFATC3 model is only a CIS-BP-mapped one. The group is weak, with a modest alt site strength drop.
E03 shows an active enhancer. The inference that losing a site reduces activity is an assumption, since NFATs can repress.
TOX3 L2G is supported (E05), but no evidence ties the NFAT site to TOX3. The gene link is the same indirect one as for the other chains.
E11 gives NFATC3 at 9.54 TPM in MCF7, so it is expressed. No NFAT activity or occupancy there is shown.

E04 shows T is the risk allele, but nothing cited says lower TOX3 raises risk. The direction is contradicted by the literature framing of E06a/E06b, where T-allele and enhancer activity are linked to risk, and the genetic evidence does not set a sign.

grades_final.reason: The QBiC group predicts alt gain, and GATA3 is reasonably picked by expression and by MCF-7 ChIP peaks over the site. But GATA3's own model z of 10.91 is far below the best model's, and the direction is only a prediction. No allele-specific ChIP is cited.
The cCRE is a dELS with high H3K27ac, and GATA3 peaks in MCF-7 are consistent with accessibility there. The z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not MCF7-specific, and no perturbation is cited.
Fine-mapping (PIP 1.00) and L2G of 0.92-0.96 for TOX3, plus proximity, give genetic prioritisation only. There is no contact, CRISPR or eQTL evidence, and GTEx shows no breast eQTL.
GATA3 expression (346 TPM) and MCF-7 ChIP peaks show the TF is present in the context. The cell-type relevance to breast cancer risk is inferred, not shown for this variant.

The T allele is strongly associated with breast cancer and the GWAS direction is consistent. Mediation by GATA3 and TOX3 is assumed, not shown. The literature quote on TOX3 is a review statement without a perturbation.
A FOXA1 ChIP peak in MCF-7 overlaps the variant, which shows occupancy. FOXA1 has no QBiC model, so the alt-gain direction is unevidenced and assumed.
The variant lies in a dELS cCRE with a FOXA1 peak in MCF-7, which is consistent with an active element. The claim that FOXA1 opens it is not tested, and the cCRE signals are not MCF7-specific.
L2G and fine-mapping prioritise TOX3, and TOX3 is the nearest gene. Nothing links the FOXA1-bound element to TOX3 through contact, perturbation or eQTL.
FOXA1 ChIP in MCF-7 supports a luminal context. No FOXA1 expression value is cited, so this is only indirect.
The GWAS association is strong and the T allele is the risk allele. The chain does not connect it to FOXA1 or to a direction of TOX3 change.

The QBiC bZIP group shows a strong alt-gain signal with consistent direction and an own MAFG model. This is a prediction only, with no ChIP or allelic assay. Choosing MAFG over MAFK (more expressed) is only loosely justified.
The variant lies in an active dELS cCRE. No small-MAF occupancy is cited and the functional role is unresolved.
L2G and proximity point to TOX3. No data link a MAF site to TOX3.
The TPM values show MAFK, MAFG and MAFB are expressed in MCF7. No occupancy is shown, so this is only expression context.
The T allele GWAS association is cited, but a MAF-mediated mechanism is not supported. The chain itself calls it a hypothesis.
The Rel group predicts alt loss. NFATC3 is chosen by expression, but its own z of -4.28 is the weakest in the group. The prediction is in vitro only.
The dELS cCRE is active, but the cited evidence says nothing about NFAT. The effect direction is stated as uncertain.
L2G and proximity prioritise TOX3 generally. Nothing ties an NFAT site to TOX3.
NFATC3 expression of 9.54 TPM in MCF7 is shown, but no NFAT occupancy at the element is cited.
The cited GWAS evidence does not set the sign of the TOX3 change this chain needs. A loss-of-binding, lowered-activity mechanism for a risk allele is untested.

next_experiment: Re-analyse the existing ENCODE MCF-7 ChIP-seq reads at chr16:52565276 for allelic imbalance in GATA3 (ENCSR000BST, ENCSR000EWV, ENCSR423RTK) and FOXA1 (ENCSR126YEB), after confirming MCF7 is heterozygous at the site.
